statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) — Suspicious activity reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: Neutral — 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements may be implicated, but the facts do not establish that a covered financial institution detected a reportable “suspicious transaction” or that any SAR-filing trigger/threshold was met.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates that the Secretary require “financial institutions” to report “any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation,” and provides related protections (e.g., safe harbor and confidentiality). To determine applicability, the facts must show (1) a covered “financial institution” subject to BSA SAR rules, and (2) the occurrence/detection of a “suspicious transaction” meeting regulatory criteria/thresholds (as implemented by Treasury/FinCEN regulations under § 5318(g)). Here, the fact pattern describes only an entity customer (SYN_bff38cd5) and a list of ACH/wire transactions with amounts mostly ~$8.8k–$40.8k and an ‘enhanced’ risk rating, but it does not identify any bank/MSB/broker-dealer/other covered financial institution, does not state that the institution formed suspicion of illegality (e.g., money laundering, structuring, fraud), and does not provide facts showing the transactions are “relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation” as required by 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g). Because the statutory element of a covered financial institution’s obligation to report a suspicious transaction cannot be confirmed from the provided facts, the statute’s suspicious activity reporting requirements cannot be determined to clearly apply or clearly not apply on this record. Contiguous phrase in answer: “31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements”.
